what_its_for: Tafasitamab-cxix is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of blood cancer called diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) that has come back or did not respond to other treatments. It is used in adults whose cancer cannot be treated with a stem cell transplant. It is always given together with another medicine called lenalidomide (Revlimid).
how_to_take: This medicine is given to you by a nurse or doctor as an IV infusion (a drip into your vein) at a clinic or hospital. You will NOT give this medicine to yourself at home. Each infusion takes several hours, so plan to spend time at the clinic on treatment days. You will be given other medicines before your infusion to help prevent reactions, such as fever or chills. Do not miss your scheduled appointments.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the exact dose based on your body weight in kilograms. The typical schedule is: Week 1 through Week 3 of Cycle 1, you receive an infusion on Days 1, 4, 8, 15, and 22. Starting in Cycle 2 and beyond (each cycle is 28 days), you receive infusions on Days 1, 8, 15, and 22. You may receive up to 12 treatment cycles with lenalidomide, and then continue tafasitamab alone if your cancer is responding. Your doctor will adjust or stop your treatment if you have side effects.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given by healthcare staff at a clinic, missed doses are managed by your care team. If you cannot make it to a scheduled infusion appointment, call your doctor or clinic as soon as possible to reschedule. Do not try to skip doses without talking to your doctor, as keeping your treatment schedule is very important for the medicine to work properly.
storage: You do not store this medicine at home. The clinic or pharmacy prepares and stores it. If you have any questions about storage, ask your healthcare team.
what_to_avoid: Avoid crowds and people who are sick, because this medicine can lower your ability to fight infections. Wash your hands often. Do not get any live vaccines (such as live flu or shingles vaccines) during treatment without asking your doctor first. Avoid becoming pregnant while on treatment and for at least 3 months after your last dose, as this medicine may harm an unborn baby. Women of childbearing age should use effective birth control. Also follow all guidelines for lenalidomide, the other medicine you are taking, as it has very strict pregnancy prevention rules.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher, chills, or signs of infection; severe allergic reactions such as difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a racing heartbeat; infusion reactions during or after your drip such as flushing, low blood pressure, or dizziness; unusual bleeding or bruising; very low energy or extreme tiredness; mouth sores that prevent you from eating or drinking; signs of nerve problems such as numbness or tingling; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Tafasitamab-cxix works by attaching to a protein called CD19 found on the surface of cancer cells and helping your immune system destroy those cells. It does not cure cancer in all patients, but in clinical studies it helped shrink tumors and keep the cancer from growing for a period of time. Your doctor will monitor your response with regular blood tests and scans. It may take several weeks to months before you and your doctor can tell how well the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not become pregnant during treatment or for at least 3 months after your last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 3 months after your last dose. Talk to your doctor about effective birth control options. Older adults (age 65 and over): This medicine has been used in older adults. Your doctor will watch you closely for side effects. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor about any kidney or liver conditions, as this may affect how your body handles the medicine. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children.
